run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:47:09Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend-proxy RequestErrorRate alert is explained by a recurring Chaos Mesh network partition between checkout and email in namespace otel-demo. The Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition in namespace chaos-mesh spawned a new NetworkChaos object every minute from 01:46:59 to at least 01:53:59, each one applying a ~55 s partition to pods email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w, email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn and checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs (all three named in the 'Successfully apply chaos' / 'Successfully recover chaos' events), with matching PodNetworkChaos 'Updated' events in otel-demo. While that partition was active, checkout's HTTP POST to the email Service (ClusterIP 100.67.49.77:8080) failed with 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout' after 30 s in its own spans and its own container log, so PlaceOrder ran 26–55 s; the frontend request therefore exceeded the 15 s proxy deadline and frontend-proxy's own ingress spans recorded HTTP 504 errors. frontend-proxy's own ERROR span count rose from a 1–4 per-10-min background to 26.3 (01:49:09), 116.8 (01:53:09) and a peak of 218.9 (01:57:09), and its 2-minute error increase jumped from ≤2.7 to 29.3 at 01:48:30 — immediately after the first partition at 01:46:59. All pods were Running/Ready with restartCount 0, both email endpoints were present, and every flagd fault flag in ConfigMap flagd-config was set to defaultVariant 'off', so pod failure, endpoint loss and flag-based fault injection are not supported by the evidence. Checked and without error evidence of their own in this window: email server spans (no email series in the ERROR-by-service result) and frontend (0 ERROR spans). The Chaos Mesh object specs could not be read (see gaps), so the exact partition parameters and the Schedule's own creation time remain unknown.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's ERROR-status span count (10-min increase) rose from a background of 0–4.4 before 01:47:09 to 26.3 at 01:49:09, 80.4 at 01:51:09, 116.8 at 01:53:09 and a peak of 218.9 at 01:57:09, while STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans fell from 13,243 at 01:47:09 to 4,075 at 02:01:09.
A 2-minute increase query for frontend-proxy STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans shows ≤2.7 per 2 min up to 01:46:30, then 29.3 at 01:48:30 and sustained 28–72 per 2 min through 01:57:00.

The frontend-proxy error spans are on operation 'ingress' with status_tags http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR and duration ~15,000,000 µs (15 s); each has a paired 'router frontend egress' client span with status error=true, http.status_code=0 and the same ~15 s duration, and the parent load-generator POST spans carry http.status_code=504.

In the sampled failing traces the frontend POST /api/checkout spans lasted 26.5–54.8 s (returning http.status_code 200), and in trace 10f92b2c323e63dfefd5f29aa9f1be2e the checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder span lasted 54.8 s with its child checkout 'HTTP POST' span also 54.8 s, while the email server span POST /send_order_confirmation for that call lasted only 3.65 ms.

checkout's failing 'HTTP POST' spans carry error=true and the exact diagnostic otel.status_description 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout' with duration 30,000,372–30,000,772 µs, and their parent oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans run ~30.1–30.4 s.
Service email in namespace otel-demo has ClusterIP 100.67.49.77 on port 8080 (targetPort 8080), which is the address in the checkout dial-timeout error.

The checkout pod's own container log contains repeated lines 'failed to send order confirmation to "<user>@example.com": failed POST to email service: Post "http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation": dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout' between 01:53:40 and 01:54:48, followed by a burst of successful 'order confirmation email sent' lines at 01:53:54–01:53:58.

Chaos Mesh Schedule 'otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition' in namespace chaos-mesh emitted 'Create new object' (Spawned) events at 01:46:59, 01:47:59, 01:48:59, 01:49:59, 01:50:59, 01:51:59, 01:52:59 and 01:53:59; each spawned NetworkChaos (jdmmj, hddgv, mznpj, zl9p2, 7rvkf, 8p7rs, 4f5lv, 5c2dr) logged 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w', '.../email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn' and '.../checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs' at start and 'Successfully recover chaos' for the same three pods ~55 s later (TimeUp at 01:47:54, 01:48:54, 01:49:54, 01:50:54, 01:51:54, 01:52:54, 01:53:54).

In namespace otel-demo, 45 PodNetworkChaos 'Updated' events ('Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource') name exactly checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs, email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w and email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn, repeating on a one-minute cadence from 01:46:59 through 01:53:59.

Across all namespaces the event grouping shows 90 NetworkChaos Updated, 24 NetworkChaos Applied, 21 NetworkChaos Recovered, 8 NetworkChaos Started, 7 TimeUp and 8 Schedule Spawned events in chaos-mesh, plus 45 PodNetworkChaos Updated events in otel-demo, as the dominant event groups in the window.

The ERROR-status span increase grouped by service returned series only for frontend-proxy (peak 218.9 per 10 min) and checkout (peak 100.9 per 10 min), with steady ~1.05 background on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation and 0 for accounting, frontend and payment; no email series was returned, so email's ERROR span count is unknown rather than zero.

The 5-minute increase of email's POST /send_order_confirmation spans fell from ~180–204 at 01:40–01:44 to 87–104 during 01:52–01:56 and 0 at 02:01:20, i.e. email received noticeably fewer calls while the partition cycles were running.

All 22 pods in otel-demo are phase Running with Ready=True and restartCount 0 (email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w and email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn started 01:13:51Z, checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs started 01:13:49Z), so no pod crash, restart or OOM is involved.

The email Service endpoint object lists both pods as ready addresses on port 8080: email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn at 100.96.2.7 (node i-0ba95c8c42c78df23) and email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w at 100.96.3.218 (node i-071e7666000f6d243), so the ClusterIP had live backends.

The flagd flag configuration in ConfigMap flagd-config has every fault flag at defaultVariant 'off', including emailMemoryLeak (off=0), paymentFailure (off=0) and paymentUnreachable (off=false); no feature-flag fault injection is switched on in this configuration.

The causal chain most consistent with the evidence is: the Chaos Mesh partition (applied by the NetworkChaos objects spawned by Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition) blocks checkout↔email traffic, checkout's POST to http://email:8080 hangs until its 30 s dial timeout, PlaceOrder therefore takes 26–55 s, the frontend /api/checkout request exceeds frontend-proxy's 15 s deadline, and frontend-proxy returns HTTP 504, which is the error signal behind RequestErrorRate.

An email application failure (crash, restart, error responses or slow handler) was considered and is not supported: both email pods are Ready with 0 restarts, the email server spans that did reach the service completed in ~3.65 ms with no error status, and no email series appeared in the ERROR-span-by-service result while errors appeared only on checkout and frontend-proxy.

Endpoint loss or pod eviction as the cause of the email connection timeouts was considered and is not supported: both email pods are listed as ready endpoint addresses on port 8080 and their pods show Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and no eviction or OOM indicators in the objects read.

Human follow-up: read and, if it is still generating partitions, suspend the Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition in namespace chaos-mesh (its NetworkChaos children are ephemeral and are recreated every minute), and confirm that frontend-proxy 504s and checkout email dial timeouts stop together with the experiment.

gaps: Chaos Mesh custom resources cannot be read with the available kinds: the Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition and its NetworkChaos children are known only from their events, so the partition's direction, mode, duration, target selector and whether the Schedule still exists (and since when) are unknown; the change_history integration is also not available.

The alert's Prometheus rule could not be inspected: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name RequestErrorRate returned no rules (no_data), so the exact alert expression and the denominator behind the reported 0.2444444444444444 error rate are unknown.

Both email containers returned no log lines at all for 01:44–02:05 (lines_read 0 for email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w and email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn), so email-side behavior during the partition is unknown, not shown to be clean.

A networkpolicies query for namespace otel-demo returned no objects; that query matching nothing is not proof that no policy existed during the incident, so a policy-based contribution is neither confirmed nor excluded.
Frontend latency has no computed pre-incident baseline here: the 26.5–54.8 s POST /api/checkout durations come from a biased Jaeger sample, so no latency trend is claimed.

Trace and span data are sampled views: the frontend-proxy spans were read from a stored over-limit result (271 spans, first 40 read) and the trace graphs omit 13 spans outside the query window, so the call chain is not complete for every request and span counts are not unique request counts.
next_steps: Inspect and suspend the Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition (namespace chaos-mesh) and verify that the per-minute NetworkChaos creation stops.

Check whether frontend-proxy 504 counts (operation 'ingress') and checkout 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout' log lines fall to zero after the experiment is suspended, as a causal confirmation.
Confirm with the team that this checkout↔email network partition is an intended fault-injection exercise before removing it.
